newsitem.title: Nepal: Nepal's prime minister wins confidence motion.
newsitem.headline: Nepal's prime minister wins confidence motion.

text.p: Nepal's Prime Minister Lokendra Bahadur Chand on Wednesday won a crucial vote of confidence in his week-old coalition that links former royalists and communists.
Parliament officials said Chand won with 113 votes against the required minimum of 103 in the 205-seat House of Representatives.

"This coalition government gives continuity to democracy... It is not a coalition against any political party or force," Chand earlier said while proposing the motion in the lower house of parliament.
Chand took power in the world's only Hindu kingdom last week after a 17-month-old centre-right coalition, undermined by charges of corruption, narrowly lost a vote of confidence.
He leads a group of rebel legislators from the Rastriya Prajatantra Party (RPP) who were part of the previous government but helped topple it.
Chand said his government would create a favourable atmosphere for private participation in Nepal's economic development and would welcome foreign investment to tap its abundant water resources.
Nepal's hydroelectric power potential is estimated at up to 83,000 megawatts. But it remains one of the world's 10 poorest countries.

The RPP's leaders helped rule the country during nearly three decades of party-less government from 1961 to 1990 that was dominated by King Birendra. Under that system, the monarch enjoyed absolute power to select and dismiss prime ministers.
Bowing to pro-democracy demonstrators in 1990, the king instituted a multi-party democracy.
The split parliament that emerged from general elections in late 1994 has yielded three coalition governments. Chand is Nepal's fifth prime minister since 1990.
Chand joined with the Unified Marxist-Leninist (UML) party, the biggest single party in the lower house of parliament, to topple the previous government and stake a claim to power.
He is required by law to prove his majority in parliament within 30 days of taking office.

His RPP faction has 10 seats in the 205-member lower house and the UML has 90. Counting other partners, the coalition commands 114 votes. The opposition Nepali Congress party holds 86 seats, with the rest controlled by independent members.
As Chand proposed the motion, the Nepali Congress instantly questioned his ability to lead a country swept by waves of political instability.
"This government cannot give political stability to the country," Congress leader Girija Prasad Koirala told the house.
Chand told reporters after the vote that he would soon expand his eight-member cabinet. He did not elaborate, but officials say communists are likely to receive three out of every five portfolios.

The major parties differ little over policy, but the communists were expected to slow economic liberalisation. The UML braked privatisation during the nine months it held power after the 1994 elections.
